deep.reconstruction:
Notation (from the previous page): P(x)=Σ_{n∈Z} x^{n^2}=1+2x+2x^4+2x^9+… (θ3 with nome x), Q(x)=Σ(-1)^n x^{n^2}=1-2x+2x^4-… (θ4), R(x)=Σ x^{(n+1/2)^2}=2x^{1/4}+2x^{9/4}+… (θ2). Product forms [7]-[12] and the duplication relations [13] P(x)Q(x)=Q(x^2)^2 and [14] P(x^2)R(x^2)=R(x)^2/2 are already established.

[16] P(x)+Q(x)=2P(x^4). Implicit step (mine): the odd-n terms cancel, leaving 2Σ_{n even} x^{n^2}=2Σ_m x^{4m^2}.

[17] P(x)-Q(x)=2R(x^4). Implicit step (mine): only the odd-n terms survive, giving 2Σ x^{(2m+1)^2}=2Σ x^{4(m+1/2)^2}.

[18] Multiplying [16] by [17] gives P^2-Q^2=4P(x^4)R(x^4). By [14] with x→x^2 this is 4·(1/2)R(x^2)^2, so P(x)^2-Q(x)^2=2R(x^2)^2.

[19] P(x)+iQ(x)=(1+i)Q(ix). [20] P(x)-iQ(x)=(1-i)P(ix). Implicit step (mine): for n even, i^{n^2}=1. For n odd, n^2≡1 (mod 8), so i^{n^2}=i. Comparing coefficients of x^{n^2} for even and odd n separately gives both identities.

[21] Multiplying [19] by [20]: P^2+Q^2=(1+i)(1-i)P(ix)Q(ix)=2Q(-x^2)^2, using [13] at argument ix. Since Q(-y)=P(y) (mine, implicit), this gives P(x)^2+Q(x)^2=2P(x^2)^2.

[22] (marginal addition) Multiplying [18] by [21] and using [14]: P^4-Q^4=4R(x^2)^2P(x^2)^2=4(R(x)^2/2)^2, so P(x)^4-Q(x)^4=R(x)^4. This is Jacobi's quartic identity θ3^4=θ2^4+θ4^4.

Consequence: P(x^2)^2 is the arithmetic mean of P(x)^2 and Q(x)^2, and by [13] Q(x^2)^2 is their geometric mean. Gauss recalls the AGM algorithm m^{(λ)}=(m^{(λ-1)}+n^{(λ-1)})/2, n^{(λ)}=sqrt(m^{(λ-1)}n^{(λ-1)}), whose common limit is the ar.-geom. mean. He cites his 'Theor[ia/Determinatio] attract.' (1818), leaving the page number blank.

Applied repeatedly, starting from m=P(x)^2, n=Q(x)^2, the algorithm gives m^{(λ)}=P(x^{2^λ})^2 and n^{(λ)}=Q(x^{2^λ})^2. Both tend to 1 as λ→∞ for |x|<1 (mine). Hence Theorem (23): AGM(P(x)^2, Q(x)^2)=1, i.e. agm(θ3^2, θ4^2)=1.

(24) Using the 1818 result ∫_0^{π/2} dφ/sqrt(a^2cos^2φ+b^2sin^2φ)=π/(2·AGM(a,b)) with a=P^2, b=Q^2: ∫_0^{2π} dφ/sqrt(P(x)^4cos^2φ+Q(x)^4sin^2φ)=2π. More generally, the integral from 0 to kπ/2 equals kπ/2 for integer k, by the π/2-symmetry of the integrand.

Gauss first wrote the integrand as 1/sqrt(cos^2/P^4+sin^2/Q^4) and struck it out. That version equals P^2Q^2 times the correct integral (with cos and sin interchanged), so it would not equal 2π.

The page serves the programme continued on the next page: parametrizing the general AGM sequence by theta functions, m^{(λ)}=μP(x^{2^λ})^2, and inverting to find x (the nome) from m and n.
errors: No mathematical errors in the final text. Each identity [16]-[22] checks as a formal power-series identity.
The struck-out integrand 1/sqrt(cos^2φ/P^4+sin^2φ/Q^4) would give 2π·P^2Q^2, not 2π. Gauss correctly replaced it.

Unstated steps: the parity/mod-8 coefficient comparisons, the use of [13] at complex argument ix, Q(-y)=P(y), and convergence of P(x^{2^λ}), Q(x^{2^λ})→1 (requires |x|<1). The last is needed for Theorem (23) but not stated.

transcription_corrections: In the marginal note, [22] reads (Px)^4 - (Qx)^4 = (Rx)^4. The machine transcription is consistent with this; the '+' in the image is a minus written with a correction stroke.

'(Theor[?] attract. et. p.     )' is a citation with a blank left for the page number. It most likely means Gauss's 'Determinatio attractionis…' (1818), where the AGM and its integral were published, i.e. '(Theor. attract. etc. p. __)'.

The struck-out first integrand is ∫dφ/sqrt(cos^2φ/(Px)^4 + sin^2φ/(Qx)^4), crossed out in the image. The correct one written to its right is ∫dφ/sqrt((Px)^4 cos^2φ + (Qx)^4 sin^2φ); 'Qx^4' in the image means (Qx)^4.

The sentence after 'vorstellt,' has an uncertain insertion above a struck phrase ('so erhellt, dass man die' deleted). The rest is roughly 'und da man ... zwei Grössenreihen ... so verbunden sind ... nennt'. 'zwei Grössen reihen' should read 'zwei Grössenreihen'.
